Name: Seed Sower
Description:
Ability id 269 (verified via cfg.GetText(TextName.AbilityNames) against the real ROM, not guessed; no existing ability-master-table entry before this package). Based on ABZB's ARM research (Seed Sower.xlsx), but the raw bytes as given in that file are BROKEN in two independent, hand-verified ways and were corrected this session; every fix was derived from live, independently cross-referenced ROM evidence, never guessed.

BUG 1 - wrong SourceBase anchor. The xlsx's own Address column claims this function starts at 0x107F10/0x107F24, but at that address the 3 internal 'bl 0x00087B58' (GetBattleVar) calls the xlsx's own instruction-text column describes actually decode (via ARMCodec.Disassemble against the real Battle.cro) to BL 0x87CB0 - a mid-function tail-branch instruction with ZERO independent BL callers anywhere else in the 0x15C000-byte file (every BL in the ROM was scanned). Disassembling the exact same unmodified bytes at 0x107DCC instead (0x158 bytes lower) makes all 3 BLs resolve to the real, 2070-caller-verified GetBattleVar at 0x87B58, and makes the 4 terrain-dispatch branches at the end resolve to 0xC8070/0xC6EE8/0xC5BC0/0xC9F4C, each confirmed this session to be a clean, live 'set terrain N + floating message' function (PUSH {R4,LR}; SUB R13,R13,#8; MOV R4,#terrain_id; MOV R12,#msg_id; STMIA; BL 0x60238; ADD R13,R13,#8; POP{R4,PC} - identical shape at all four). Conclusion: ABZB tested this snippet at a fixed scratch address (0x107DCC - also where this session's Ruin Abilities package's 'report self' function sits in ABZB's own numbering) and then hand-typed an unrelated cosmetic starting address into the spreadsheet for filing, without re-deriving the position-dependent branch encodings - not a real conflict with Ruin Abilities, since TarShot.json and Ripen.json already independently reuse the identical donor SourceBase 0x105578 for two unrelated packages; this project's installer (MechanicInstaller + CodeRelocator.RebaseCode) relocates each package to wherever real free space actually exists at install time and rewrites every branch for the true destination, so SourceBase is only the anchor needed to compute that rewrite, not a literal install address.

BUG 2 - 3 early-exit branches point at dead space regardless of anchor. Even after fixing BUG 1, the 3 conditional early-exit branches (BEQ/BNE guarding 'self is attacker', 'self is not defender', 'no damage taken') still decode to 0x107F7C, which is empty/zero-filled space in the pristine ROM at every anchor tried - not this function's own final return instruction (which sits at SourceBase+0x58, i.e. 0x107E24 under the corrected anchor). Installing it as ABZB wrote it would branch into dead space the instant Seed Sower's holder takes no damage or isn't the defender - i.e. almost every time this timing fires for a Pokemon on the field that ISN'T the holder, since ability-effect timings broadcast to every battler. Fixed by re-encoding just those 3 branch immediates (BEQ 0x0E00000A, BNE 0x0A00001A, BNE 0x0600001A) to target 0x107E24 - the function's real, verified-in-place final 'POP {R0,R1,R2,R3,R4,R5,PC}' - computed via EncodeB (a small ARM branch-immediate encoder written this session, not hand math) and round-tripped back through ARMCodec.Disassemble to confirm each one. Every other byte, including the 4 terrain tail-branches and all 3 GetBattleVar calls, is untouched. Full function re-disassembled end to end with no warnings and every branch landing on a real, live, or internally-consistent target before this package was written; also confirmed post-relocation (ApplyBattleCro on the real ROM, not just Preview) that the installed copy at its new address still resolves the 3 early-exit branches to its own real end, not the stale absolute address.

Single function, Timing 0x60 ('on being hit'): checks self is not the attacker (GetBattleVar(0x3)) and is the defender (GetBattleVar(0x4)) and actually took damage (GetBattleVar(0x4B)==0 is false, i.e. non-zero damage), then sets Grassy Terrain (r0=1, preserved across the whole check sequence via push/pop of r0 alongside the callee-saved registers) via a tail-branch (plain B, not BL) into the ROM's own real, native Grassy-Terrain-setting routine - a direct jump into existing engine code rather than reimplementing terrain-setting.
